{{nihongo|'''Ionoi Shrine'''|五百井神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Ōmi Province]].

'''Ioinoi Shrine''' (いおのいじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945}} located in Shimotoyama, {{ill|Rittō, Shiga|ar|ريتو (شيغا)|azb|ریتو، شیقا|ce|Ритто|ceb|Rittō-shi|de|Rittō|es|Rittō (Shiga)|fa|ریتو، شیگا|fi|Rittō|fr|Rittō|gl|Rittō|hy|Ռիտտո|id|Rittō, Shiga|it|Rittō|ja|栗東市|ko|릿토시|mzn|ریتو، شیگا|nl|Ritto|pl|Rittō|pt|Ritto|ro|Rittō|ru|Ритто|sv|Rittō, Shiga|tg|Ритто|tl|Rittō, Shiga|tr|Rittō|tt|Ритто|uk|Рітто|ur|رٹو، شیگا|vi|Rittō, Shiga|war|Rittō, Shiga|zh|栗東市|zh_classical|栗東市|zh_min_nan|Rittô-chhī|zh_yue|栗東|qid=Q857310}}, {{ill|Shiga Prefecture|Q131358|qid=Q131358}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}}, and under the {{ill|Q712534|lt=former shrine ranking system}} it was classified as a {{ill|Son-sha|ja|村社|qid=Q134917284}}. The {{ill|Chartrand|ru|Шартран|qid=Q1067875}} is the “descending wisteria” motif.<ref name="神社庁">[http://www.shiga-jinjacho.jp/ycBBS/Board.cgi/02_jinja_db/db/ycDB_02jinja-pc-detail.html?mode:view=1&view:oid=369 Ioinoi Shrine] (Shiga Prefecture Association of Shinto Shrines).</ref>

=== Enshrined deity ===
The shrine enshrines the following single deity<ref name="神社庁"/>:
* {{ill|Kimata-no-Kami|ja|木俣神|zh|木俁神|qid=Q11092833}} – also known as “Mii-no-Kami.” A deity statue dating from the {{ill|Heian period|Q193292|qid=Q193292}} (designated a Tangible Cultural Property of Shiga Prefecture) has been handed down.

=== History ===
=== Founding ===
The date of founding is unknown. The shrine precincts are located on the southwestern foothills of Mount Anyōji; on the summit stand the inner shrine (Sannō Shrine) and the Ryūō Shrine. This inner shrine is said to be the place where the enshrined deity descended.<ref name="神社庁"/>{{Sfn|Ioinoi Shrine (Heibonsha)|1991}} There is also a tradition that the shrine was worshipped by the Ashii clan.<ref name="神社庁"/>

In the late {{ill|Kamakura period|Q236205|qid=Q236205}} anthology *Fubokushō*, the Kanasatsu River flowing in front of the shrine precincts appears as “Ihonoi River,” leading to a theory that this shrine was worshipped as a guardian deity of the irrigation well supplying water there.{{Sfn|Ioinoi Shrine (Heibonsha)|1991}}

=== Overview ===
According to shrine tradition, in the first year of {{ill|Ninju|Q1373077|qid=Q1373077}} ({{ill|851|ab|851|af|851|als|851|am|851 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|851|ar|851|ary|851|ast|851|avk|851|az|851|azb|۸۵۱ (میلادی)|bcl|851|be|851|be_x_old|851|bg|851|bn|৮৫১|bpy|মারি ৮৫১|br|851|bs|851.|ca|851|cdo|851 nièng|ce|851 шо|ceb|851|ckb|٨٥١|crh|851|cs|851|csb|851|cv|851|cy|851|da|851|de|851|el|851|eml|851|eo|851|es|851|et|851|eu|851|fa|۸۵۱ (میلادی)|fi|851|fo|851|fr|851|fy|851|ga|851|gan|851年|gd|851|gl|851|gv|851|he|851|hi|851|hr|851.|ht|851 (almanak jilyen)|hu|851|hy|851|id|851|ilo|851|io|851|it|851|ja|851年|jv|851|ka|851|kaa|851|kk|851 жыл|ko|851년|la|851|lb|851|lij|851|lmo|851|lt|851 m.|lv|851. gads|map_bms|851|mdf|851|mg|851|mhr|851|mk|851|mr|इ.स. ८५१|mrj|851 и|ms|851|mzn|۸۵۱|nah|851|nap|851|nds|851|new|सन् ८५१|nl|851|nn|851|no|851|nrm|851|nso|851|oc|851|or|୮୫୧|os|851-æм аз|pl|851|pnb|851|pt|851|qu|851|ro|851|ru|851 год|rue|851|sa|८५१|scn|851|sd|851ع|se|851|sh|851.|shn|851|si|851|sk|851|sl|851|smn|851|sq|851|sr|851|su|851|sv|851|sw|851|tg|Соли 851|th|พ.ศ. 1394|tk|851|tl|851|tly|851|tr|851|tt|851 ел|uk|851|ur|851ء|uz|851|vec|851|vi|851|war|851|wuu|851年|xmf|851|zh|851年|zh_min_nan|851 nî|zh_yue|851年|qid=Q29966}}), in January, the shrine was granted the divine rank of Senior Sixth Rank, Upper Grade.{{Sfn|Ioinoi Shrine (Heibonsha)|1991}} According to the *{{ill|Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku|cs|Nihon Montoku Tennó Džicuroku|de|Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku|es|Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku|ff|Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku|fr|Nihon Montoku tennō jitsuroku|ja|日本文徳天皇実録|ko|일본문덕천황실록|pt|Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku|zh|日本文德天皇實錄|qid=Q1052905}}*, a simultaneous promotion of various deities to Senior Sixth Rank, Upper Grade took place on January 27 of that year.

In the *{{ill|Engishiki|ar|إنجيشيكي (كتاب ياباني)|de|Engishiki|es|Engishiki|fr|Engishiki|he|אנגישיקי|id|Engishiki|it|Engishiki|ja|延喜式|ko|엔기시키|min|Engishiki|mr|इंगिशिकी|nl|Engishiki|pt|Engishiki|ru|Энгисики|simple|Engishiki|tr|Engishiki|uk|Енґісікі|zh|延喜式|qid=Q1342448}}* {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}} compiled in the fifth year of {{ill|Enchō|Q1327274|qid=Q1327274}} ({{ill|927|Q30470|qid=Q30470}}), the shrine is listed as “Ashii Shrine” in {{ill|Kurita District, Shiga|ja|栗太郡|zh|栗太郡|qid=Q6446084}}, {{ill|Ōmi Province|Q843882|qid=Q843882}}, and is included among the {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}}.{{Sfn|Ioinoi Shrine (Heibonsha)|1991}} In manuscript copies of this register, the reading of “Ashii” is glossed as “Ihonoino.”

As mentioned above, in the late Kamakura period *Fubokushō* the name “Ihonoi River” appears, and it is said that from around the end of the {{ill|Middle Ages|Q12554|qid=Q12554}} the shrine name came to be written as “Ioinoi.”{{Sfn|Ioinoi Shrine (Heibonsha)|1991}}

يىلى|uk|2013|ur|2013ء|uz|2013|vec|2013|vi|2013|vls|2013|vo|2013|wa|2013|war|2013|wuu|2013年|xmf|2013|yi|2013|za|2013 nienz|zea|2013|zgh|2013|zh|2013年|zh_classical|二〇一三年|zh_min_nan|2013 nî|zh_yue|2013年|zu|2013|qid=Q1998}} ({{ill|Heisei era|Q234510|qid=Q234510}} 25), a landslide occurred on the slope behind the shrine precincts due to the effects of {{ill|Typhoon Man-yi (2013)|Q14941852|qid=Q14941852}}, and the shrine buildings, including the main hall and worship hall, were almost completely destroyed. As a result, the divine spirit was transferred to a {{ill|Otabisho|Q11489117|qid=Q11489117}}, and rituals have continued there (as of May 2014). The deity statue that had been enshrined in the main hall was excavated from the soil two weeks after the landslide; later its artistic value was reappraised, and in {{ill|2015|Q2002|qid=Q2002}} (Heisei 27) it was designated a Tangible Cultural Property of Shiga Prefecture.<ref>[https://www.sankei.com/article/20140506-6OMGSUKO6FJEXCU5R4BG3B6XCM/ “Ritto’s typhoon-damaged Ioinoi Shrine ‘Grand Festival’ Shiga”] (Sankei News, May 6, 2014).<br />[http://kyoto-np.co.jp/sightseeing/article/20151221000044 “A strange fate: damaged deity statue becomes cultural property – buried by landslide, re-evaluated –”] (Kyoto Shimbun, December 21, 2015).<br />[http://mainichi.jp/articles/20151222/ddl/k25/040/545000c “Nine new prefectural cultural properties: Takashima’s Ninigi Shrine and Ritto’s wooden seated male deity, etc. / Shiga”] (Mainichi Shimbun, December 22, 2015).</ref>

=== Cultural properties ===
=== Shiga Prefecture designated cultural properties ===
* Tangible Cultural Properties
** Wooden seated male deity statue, 1 figure (sculpture) – Heian period work. Made in the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=ichiboku-zukuri}} technique, with a height of 33.8 centimeters. Designated on December 18, 2015 (Heisei 27).<ref>[http://www.city.ritto.shiga.jp/hakubutsukan/sub315.htm Shiga Prefecture designated cultural properties located in Ritto City] (Ritto City website).</ref><ref>{{PDFlink|[http://www.pref.shiga.lg.jp/edu/files/03dansinzazou.pdf Sculpture section]}} (Shiga Prefectural Board of Education website).</ref>
** Black-lacquered, gilt-bronze-mounted creeping oak-pattern saddle (craft) – Kamakura period work. Designated as a city cultural property in 1996 (Heisei 8) on December 6 under the name “Wooden creeping oak-pattern saddle,”<ref>[http://www.city.ritto.shiga.jp/hakubutsukan/sub216.htm Ritto City designated cultural properties] (Ritto City website).</ref> and designated as a prefectural cultural property on December 24, 2019 (Reiwa 1).<ref>{{PDFlink|[https://www.pref.shiga.lg.jp/file/attachment/5147872.pdf Shiga Prefectural Board of Education Notice No. 8, December 24, Reiwa 1]}} (Shiga Prefecture website).</ref>
